topic: digital governance for community elderly-care services

cases.finding: A unified service ledger helped staff compare registered demand with actual meal delivery records and identify older residents who missed repeated meals.
cases.evidence_boundary: The record was useful only when service providers updated delivery status on the same day.
cases.risk: If cancellation and hospitalisation information is not updated, the ledger may overestimate unmet demand.

cases.finding: Regular visit records made it easier to prioritise residents living alone, especially when visit frequency, emergency contacts, and recent health notes were kept together.
cases.evidence_boundary: The approach depends on consistent definitions of visit completion and risk level.
cases.risk: Sensitive health and family information should be visible only to authorised staff.

recommendations: start with a bounded service catalogue
keep one resident profile across providers
record service completion and follow-up results
review high-risk cases through offline staff meetings
